# Ambient light installation via map lamp

> **[Unverified]** This page rests on a single community report. Cross-check before relying on it.

> Items marked **[Partial]** are only partly confirmed by the source and need more work. They stay in the review queue and are firmed up, corrected or removed as more sources come in.

## Summary

[Partial] Modify the map light counsel to fit a shortened PUSH TOP Bic pen and install an LD1 Amber LED. [t984]

## Procedure

> **[Partial]** Needs more work: the verifier could confirm only part of this procedure (the steps marked [Partial], or whether the list is complete). Steps or precautions may be wrong or missing; read the source thread before relying on it. Later runs fill it in as more sources are found.

1. Pull down the map light or ceiling counsel.
2. [Partial] Modify the counsel to fit the LED.
3. Center and drill a hole in the counsel.
4. Use a Dremel to bevel the edge of the drilled hole.
5. Disassemble your push top Bic pen.
6. Test fitment before starting further cuts.
7. [Partial] Cut about 1/4 inch off the end of the main tube and the cap piece.
8. Cut another 1/16 inch off the end cap to allow room for the LED.
9. Slide the shortened end cap back into the main tube section.
10. Center your diffuser (Bic pen) over the hole in the counsel.
11. [Partial] Glue the Bic pen assembly in place.
12. Install your LD1 amber LED and wire it up.
13. Secure the wiring with electrical tape to the frame of the counsel.
14. Tap the power source off of your temperature gauge mod.
15. Reinstall your ceiling counsel.

_Procedure reported by [t984]. Photos of this job are in the source: <https://www.xterranation.org/index.php?threads/how-to-ambient-light-macguyver-mod.2898/>_

## Tips & gotchas

- [Partial] Use a Dremel to bevel the drilled hole edge so light reflects less and looks stealthy. [t984]
- [Partial] Slide the cut end piece of the pen into the main tube section before gluing. [t984]
- Use a PUSH TOP Bic pen because the regular inside diameter is too small. [t984]
- Bevel the edge of the drilled hole with a Dremel to prevent light reflection and keep it stealthy. [t984]
